title: Bangkok Underwater: 12 Inches of Rain Floods Thailand's Capital
summary:
Imagine rain so heavy that it fills your whole street like a swimming pool. That's what happened in Bangkok, the capital of Thailand. Since Thursday, more than 300mm (12 inches) of rain has fallen — that's like dumping a giant bucket over the whole city. Now roads are underwater.

All 50 districts of Bangkok have been declared emergency zones. That means the city is officially in a disaster. The governor, Chadchart Sittipunt, says the east side got hit the hardest. "Every canal is now filled," he said.

A 67-year-old woman named Somkid Pheuk-ngam lives near a canal north of central Bangkok. She told a news agency, "The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now." She has closed her shop for two days.

People have been told to stay home. If they live near a canal, they should move their things to higher floors. The rain has stopped for now, but the canals are still full. More heavy rain is coming this week. So far, no one has been hurt in Bangkok — and everyone hopes it stays that way.
why_it_matters: When a city floods, kids cannot get to school, parents cannot get to work and shops close — which is why cities build canals, pumps and warning systems before the water rises.

background_read: Bangkok is the capital of Thailand, a country in Southeast Asia, and millions of people live there.
Thailand has a rainy season every year, when heavy monsoon rain falls for months, and Bangkok is built on low, flat land, so water drains away slowly.
In 2011, huge floods in Thailand damaged large parts of Bangkok and forced many families to leave their homes — a disaster Thai people still remember.

perspectives.description: Somkid Pheuk-ngam says the water is at her waist level, it is hard to go out, and she has closed her shop for two days.
The governor says the east side was hit hardest and every canal is now full, so all 50 districts are being treated as emergency zones.
The rain has stopped for now and no one in Bangkok has been hurt, so people hope the city can drain the water before the next heavy rain.
